authoring.value:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064490/assets/aef99dd5276166e5c7b4fb2f716b060390b6577f2d3625dd5dc835bcec6c4856.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 3=\frac{9}{2}.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=(-5)\cdot (-2)-0\cdot 0=10.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,10\,|\cdot \frac{9}{2} \\  & =45.\end{aligned}
$$
